To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ANX 7 gene, located on human chromosome10q21, is a candidate tumor suppresser gene (TSG) for prostate cancer.

(1) ANX7 is a TSG that suppresses prostate tumor cell growth; (2) ANX7 expression is reduced in metastatic and hormone refractory prostate tumors; (3) LOH of markers at the ANX7 loci is frequent in primary prostate tumors.

ANX7, an annexin family member with a known role in apoptosis, exhibits many biological and molecular features of a candidate tumor suppressive gene, including a significant reduction of tumor cell growth and a high incidence of loss of heterozygozity (LOH) and loss of protein expression in prostate cancer specimens.
